openAPIV3Schema.description:
LongContextPreset is a preset for vLLM deployments that prioritize
max-context-per-model over throughput. Consumed by LongContextInstance.

apiVersion.description:
APIVersion defines the versioned schema of this representation of an object.
Servers should convert recognized schemas to the latest internal value, and
may reject unrecognized values.
More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#resources

kind.description:
Kind is a string value representing the REST resource this object represents.
Servers may infer this from the endpoint the client submits requests to.
Cannot be updated.
In CamelCase.
More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#types-kinds

spec.description:
LongContextPresetSpec is a preset tuned for maximum context length per model.
It mirrors ModelPresetSpec field-for-field and adds two long-context-specific
fields. The new type exists so the existing ModelPreset semantics are
untouched while opinionated defaults (KV quantization, prefix caching) ship
here.

compilationConfig.description:
CompilationConfig is passed through VERBATIM as the value of vLLM's
--compilation-config flag. Same raw-pass-through convention as
LimitMmPerPrompt and SpeculativeConfig above.

Free-form string rather than a structured type on purpose: vLLM accepts
either a JSON object (e.g. `{"level":0}` or
`{"cudagraph_capture_sizes":[1,2,4]}`) or a bare optimization level
(e.g. `3`), so a struct-typed field would reject values vLLM accepts.
Empty = flag omitted.

NOT VALIDATED AT ADMISSION: this repo ships no admission webhook (no
config/webhook, no *_webhook.go) and CEL/XValidation cannot parse JSON,
so a malformed value surfaces as a vLLM start-up failure
(CrashLoopBackOff), not an apply-time rejection. This matches the
existing behaviour of limitMmPerPrompt and speculativeConfig.

Finer-grained CUDA-graph control — e.g. shrinking capture sizes rather
than disabling graphs outright — belongs in this field, which is why
there is no separate cudagraphCaptureSizes field to keep in sync.

cpuOffloadGiB.description:
CPUOffloadGiB enables vLLM's --cpu-offload-gb flag, moving evicted KV
blocks to host RAM instead of recomputing on the next prefix hit.
Helps repeat-prefix TTFT at long context. 0 = disabled.

enableChunkedPrefill.description:
EnableChunkedPrefill toggles vLLM's chunked-prefill scheduler. Sidesteps
the multimodal budget check on v0.20+ when MaxNumBatchedTokens is left
at default. Useful for long-context throughput too.

enableLora.description: Enable LoRA adapter serving in vLLM

enablePrefixCaching.description:
EnablePrefixCaching enables vLLM's RadixAttention-style automatic prefix
caching. Tri-state pointer semantics:
  - nil      → use kubebuilder default (true at admission time)
  - &false   → explicitly disabled
  - &true    → explicitly enabled
The pointer type fixes the kubebuilder default+omitempty trap that
previously made it impossible to disable the field once defaulted on.

enforceEager.description:
EnforceEager disables CUDA graph capture and runs the model in eager
PyTorch mode (vLLM's --enforce-eager). It costs throughput, but on some
GPUs it is the only known-stable configuration: on RTX PRO 6000
(sm_120) the default CUDA-graph path wedges the device with Xid 79
after ~72 s, while --enforce-eager survived a >1 h soak. Exposing it
here makes that mitigation GitOps-expressible instead of a hand-edited
Deployment.

Tri-state pointer, matching the EnablePrefixCaching convention:
  - nil    -> flag not emitted (vLLM default: CUDA graphs enabled)
  - &false -> flag not emitted, but explicitly declared
  - &true  -> --enforce-eager emitted as a bare flag (no value)
There is deliberately NO kubebuilder default: defaulting this on would
silently cost throughput on every healthy GPU. The pointer type also
avoids the kubebuilder default+omitempty trap documented on
EnablePrefixCaching.

env.description:
Env supplies vLLM container environment variables. Instance spec.env wins
on duplicate names. Use valueFrom for references, not literal secrets.

items.description: EnvVar represents an environment variable present in a Container.

name.description:
Name of the environment variable.
May consist of any printable ASCII characters except '='.

value.description:
Variable references $(VAR_NAME) are expanded
using the previously defined environment variables in the container and
any service environment variables. If a variable cannot be resolved,
the reference in the input string will be unchanged. Double $$ are reduced
to a single $, which allows for escaping the $(VAR_NAME) syntax: i.e.
"$$(VAR_NAME)" will produce the string literal "$(VAR_NAME)".
Escaped references will never be expanded, regardless of whether the variable
exists or not.
Defaults to "".

valueFrom.description: Source for the environment variable's value. Cannot be used if value is not empty.

configMapKeyRef.description: Selects a key of a ConfigMap.

name.description:
Name of the referent.
This field is effectively required, but due to backwards compatibility is
allowed to be empty. Instances of this type with an empty value here are
almost certainly wrong.
More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/names/#names

optional.description: Specify whether the ConfigMap or its key must be defined

fieldRef.description:
Selects a field of the pod: supports metadata.name, metadata.namespace, `metadata.labels['<KEY>']`, `metadata.annotations['<KEY>']`,
spec.nodeName, spec.serviceAccountName, status.hostIP, status.podIP, status.podIPs.

apiVersion.description: Version of the schema the FieldPath is written in terms of, defaults to "v1".

fieldPath.description: Path of the field to select in the specified API version.

fileKeyRef.description:
FileKeyRef selects a key of the env file.
Requires the EnvFiles feature gate to be enabled.

key.description:
The key within the env file. An invalid key will prevent the pod from starting.
The keys defined within a source may consist of any printable ASCII characters except '='.
During Alpha stage of the EnvFiles feature gate, the key size is limited to 128 characters.

optional.description:
Specify whether the file or its key must be defined. If the file or key
does not exist, then the env var is not published.
If optional is set to true and the specified key does not exist,
the environment variable will not be set in the Pod's containers.

If optional is set to false and the specified key does not exist,
an error will be returned during Pod creation.

path.description:
The path within the volume from which to select the file.
Must be relative and may not contain the '..' path or start with '..'.

volumeName.description: The name of the volume mount containing the env file.

resourceFieldRef.description:
Selects a resource of the container: only resources limits and requests
(limits.cpu, limits.memory, limits.ephemeral-storage, requests.cpu, requests.memory and requests.ephemeral-storage) are currently supported.

containerName.description: Container name: required for volumes, optional for env vars

divisor.description: Specifies the output format of the exposed resources, defaults to "1"

secretKeyRef.description: Selects a key of a secret in the pod's namespace

key.description: The key of the secret to select from.  Must be a valid secret key.

name.description:
Name of the referent.
This field is effectively required, but due to backwards compatibility is
allowed to be empty. Instances of this type with an empty value here are
almost certainly wrong.
More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/names/#names

optional.description: Specify whether the Secret or its key must be defined

kvCacheDtype.description:
KVCacheDtype controls vLLM's --kv-cache-dtype flag. Required for this
preset type — long-context deployments must opt in to a specific KV
cache quantization. FP8 KV roughly halves KV memory at long context,
approximately doubling max-model-len at the same VRAM budget; NVFP4
(4-bit) goes further (~4× density) but is bleeding-edge — not all
vLLM versions support it. Use `auto` to let vLLM pick a default
compatible with the weight quantization.
fp8_e4m3 is chosen as the default because vLLM rejects fp8_e5m2 on
FP8/NVFP4 weight checkpoints; e4m3 works with both BF16 and quantized
weights. See issue #7.

kvCacheDtypeSkipLayers.description:
KVCacheDtypeSkipLayers exempts a layer group from KVCacheDtype
quantization via vLLM's --kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers flag, e.g.
"sliding_window". Gemma 4's sliding-window layers are the
FP8-KV-quantization-sensitive ones per vLLM FP8-KV guidance; this lets
presets keep them at native dtype while global layers stay fp8_e4m3.
Empty = flag omitted (all layers use KVCacheDtype).

kvOffloadBackend.description:
KVOffloadBackend selects an external KV-offload store. Empty/"none"
disables; "lmcache" reserves the slot for an in-pod LMCache sidecar
(wired in a follow-up PR — this PR adds the field only).

kvOffloadSize.description:
KVOffloadSize is the host-RAM budget for the external KV cache, in GiB.
Used as the LMCache buffer size when KVOffloadBackend == "lmcache".
0 = backend default.

limitMmPerPrompt.description:
LimitMmPerPrompt controls vLLM's --limit-mm-per-prompt flag, passed
through verbatim as a raw JSON object string (e.g. `{"image":0,"audio":0}`).
Text-only serving wastes VRAM on multimodal profiling; zeroing every
modality here reclaims that memory for the KV cache. Empty = flag
omitted (vLLM's own multimodal defaults apply).

livenessProbe.description:
ProbeConfig is the tunable subset of a k8s probe.
All three fields (initialDelaySeconds, periodSeconds, failureThreshold) flow
through to the rendered Pod spec for both liveness and readiness probes.

loraModules.description: LoRA module name and path format: name=path

mambaBackend.description:
MambaBackend controls vLLM's --mamba-backend flag (the Mamba selective
state-update backend). OPTIONAL and unset by default: when empty, no
--mamba-backend arg is rendered, so existing presets are byte-identical.
No kubebuilder default, for the same zero-blast-radius reason.

On sm_120 (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell) `flashinfer` is recommended per vLLM
issue #37431. Left as a free-form string rather than an enum: vLLM 0.27.1
parses --mamba-backend as a plain string and only resolves it against
MambaBackendEnum (triton/flashinfer/cpu, case-insensitively) at engine
init, so pinning an enum here would risk rejecting a backend valid in a
different vLLM build without adding real safety.

mambaCacheMode.description:
MambaCacheMode controls vLLM's --mamba-cache-mode flag for hybrid
Mamba/attention models (e.g. NemotronH). OPTIONAL and unset by default:
when empty, no --mamba-cache-mode arg is rendered, so every existing
preset renders byte-identically to pre-#404 behavior. There is
deliberately NO kubebuilder default — a default would widen the rendered
args for every current preset.

Why it exists (issue #404): with --enable-prefix-caching and no explicit
--mamba-cache-mode, vLLM silently auto-selects `all` on NemotronH (it
declares SupportsMambaPrefixCaching). Presets that force Model Runner V2
(DSpark speculative decoding) then hit an assertion at mamba_mixer2.py
because MambaHybridAttnMetadata never passes prev_last_scheduled_idx
(upstream vllm-project/vllm#52317). Setting `align` avoids the `all`-mode
branch; a probe pod proved DSpark spec-decode works with it (56/69 draft
tokens accepted, 81%). Follows the KVCacheDtype field convention.

The enum mirrors vLLM 0.27.1's MambaCacheMode literal exactly
(vllm/config/cache.py: Literal["all", "align", "none"]).

maxNumBatchedTokens.description:
MaxNumBatchedTokens caps tokens per scheduling iteration.
Required >= max_tokens_per_mm_item for multimodal models on vLLM v0.20+
(Gemma 4: 2496). Empty/0 = vLLM default (2048 on v0.20).

maxNumSeqs.description:
MaxNumSeqs caps vLLM's scheduler concurrency (--max-num-seqs). The
serving workload is 1-3 concurrent requests; the vLLM default (256+)
wastes CUDA-graph capture time and reserved memory. 0 = flag omitted.

readinessProbe.description:
ProbeConfig is the tunable subset of a k8s probe.
All three fields (initialDelaySeconds, periodSeconds, failureThreshold) flow
through to the rendered Pod spec for both liveness and readiness probes.

reasoningParser.description:
ReasoningParser selects vLLM's --reasoning-parser. For Gemma 4 thinking
models this must be "gemma4" so the \thought ... reasoning channel is
separated from response content; without it the chain-of-thought leaks
into content and tool_use blocks fail to surface.

servedModelName.description:
ServedModelName overrides the name vLLM advertises to clients (see
the corresponding field on ModelPresetSpec for full docs). Useful for
keeping a stable client-facing name (e.g. `google/gemma-4-31B-it`)
regardless of whether the long-context preset's backend weights are
NVFP4 or BF16.

speculativeConfig.description:
SpeculativeConfig is a raw JSON configuration for vLLM's speculative decoding.
Example: {"method":"ngram","num_speculative_tokens":4,"prompt_lookup_min":2,"prompt_lookup_max":5}

startupProbe.description:
ProbeConfig is the tunable subset of a k8s probe.
All three fields (initialDelaySeconds, periodSeconds, failureThreshold) flow
through to the rendered Pod spec for both liveness and readiness probes.
